```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ef_moves()` uses local MOVES rate data to evaluate running-exhaust emission
factors. It runs in R on Linux, macOS and Windows. There is no database connection,
SQL query, Java process, network download or MOVES installation involved in
evaluating factors.

## Vehicle type, fuel and age

These inputs are explicit arguments of `ef_moves()`:

| Argument | Meaning | Bundled reference data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_type_id` | MOVES vehicle category | all 13 on-road types |
| `fuel_type_id` | MOVES fuel type | every valid combination (names accepted) |
| `model_year` | Vehicle manufacturing year | 2000--2025 |
| `road_type_id` | MOVES road category | `5`: urban unrestricted |
| `temperature` | Temperature in degrees C | 10, 20 or 30 |
| `rel_humidity` | Relative humidity in percent | 50 |

Use `moves_vehicles()` to list the available source-type and fuel combinations
with their names and IDs. The bundled data include 38 of the 48 MOVES6-valid
vehicle/fuel combinations. The five fuels are gasoline, diesel, E-85, CNG and
electricity; not every fuel is valid for every vehicle type. Combinations with
no modelled running-exhaust output, such as heavy electric trucks and CNG or
electric motor homes, are not listed.

Vehicle age is the inventory year minus `model_year`. The bundled inventory
year is 2025, so `model_year = 2020` represents a five-year-old vehicle.
For other datasets, choose the inventory year with `select = list(yearID = ...)`.

## Use the reference factors

The small dataset shipped with VEIN contains MOVES6 running-exhaust rates for a
documented U.S. reference scenario. The selected model year describes the
vehicle's year of manufacture; `yearID` is the inventory year, which determines
vehicle age. They must not be interchanged.

```{r}
library(vein)
x <- moves_factors()
moves_vehicles()
x$runs[, c("masterVersion", "defaultDatabaseUsed", "massUnits", "distanceUnits")]
unique(x$rates[, c("yearID", "hourID", "temperature_C", "relHumidity")])
range(x$rates$modelYearID)
```

Select a vehicle and fuel by name or numeric ID. This example is a model-year
2020 diesel combination long-haul truck:

```{r}
ef_moves(
  pollutant = "NOx",
  source_type_id = "Combination Long-haul Truck",
  fuel_type_id = "Diesel Fuel",
  model_year = 2020,
  speed = c(20, 40, 60),
  temperature = 20
)
```

Here is NOx from a model-year 2020 gasoline passenger car at the hour-1 reference
conditions. Numeric input speeds use km/h; results have units of g/km.

```{r}
ef_moves("NOx", model_year = 2020, speed = c(20, 40, 60),
         factors = x, select = list(hourID = 1))
```

`temperature` (degrees C) and `rel_humidity` (percent) can select meteorological
points directly. Any remaining varying dimensions must be selected explicitly
using `select`. The function never averages together different scenarios,
model years, fuels, road types or temperatures.

The reference fleet and fuel assumptions describe the U.S. scenario recorded in
the dataset. Application to Ecuador requires a suitable vehicle/technology
mapping and local fuel, meteorology, road load and inspection assumptions.
The input metadata and production notes are installed with the data:

```{r}
system.file("extdata", "moves", "README.md", package = "vein")
```

## Speed functions for VEIN inventories

Omitting `speed` returns a function of speed giving numeric g/km. Build one
function per model year in the same order as the columns of the vehicle matrix.

```{r}
years <- c(2020, 2010)
curves <- EmissionFactorsList(lapply(years, function(y) {
  ef_moves("NOx", model_year = y, factors = x, select = list(hourID = 1))
}))
veh <- data.frame(MY2020 = c(100, 200), MY2010 = c(30, 50))
lengths <- units::set_units(c(0.5, 1), "km")
speeds <- data.frame(H1 = c(30, 50))
emissions <- emis(veh, lengths, ef = curves, speed = speeds,
                  profile = matrix(1, 1, 1), simplify = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
emissions
```

## Native bins and interpolation

The default `method = "bin"` selects the exported MOVES rate for the corresponding
speed bin. It preserves valid zeros and fails if a requested bin is absent.
Positive speeds up to 75 mph (120.7008 km/h) are accepted. Stationary idle needs
an hour-based factor and matching activity; a distance factor cannot describe it.

With `method = "linear"`, factors are interpolated between nominal MOVES bin
speeds: 2.5, 5, 10, ..., 75 mph. Both neighboring bins must exist. Extrapolation
is disabled. This is an approximation between exported rates, so speed-bin
lookup is the appropriate method for exact reproduction of the reference table.

```{r}
f <- ef_moves("NOx", model_year = 2020, factors = x,
              select = list(hourID = 1), method = "linear")
f(c(20, 40, 60))
attr(f, "moves_metadata")$scenario
```

Meteorology, model year and vehicle category are selected exactly; this first
version does not interpolate those dimensions.

## Start and evaporative factors

Start exhaust is **grams per engine start**, not g/km. Use the separate start
data and function; there is deliberately no speed argument:

```{r}
starts <- moves_start_factors()
ef_moves_start(
  "NOx", model_year = 2020,
  source_type_id = "Passenger Car", fuel_type_id = "Gasoline",
  select = list(hourID = 1)
)
```

The evaporative data contain THC permeation (process 11), fuel vapor venting
(process 12) and fuel leaks (process 13). Permeation and leaks are **g/vehicle**;
venting is **per profile event** and retains its MOVES temperature-profile ID.

```{r}
evap <- moves_evap_factors()
ef_moves_evap(
  "THC", model_year = 2020, process = "all",
  source_type_id = "Passenger Car", fuel_type_id = "Gasoline",
  select = list(hourID = 1)
)
```

These event-based factors cannot be passed to `emis()`, whose factors are g/km.
Multiply them by matching start or vehicle activity, and handle venting with its
temperature profile. Start and evaporative data are separate MOVES runs; their
provenance is recorded in `movesrun_events.csv`.

## Supply additional local data

Data producers can run MOVES once and export running-exhaust `RatePerDistance`
and `MOVESRun` tables. R users only need those local files or a saved RDS object.
The importer reads units from `MOVESRun`, preserves all original rate-table
dimensions, converts pollutant mass rates to g/km, and checks for duplicate keys
and missing provenance. It supports plain or gzip-compressed CSV and TSV files.

```{r eval=FALSE}
x <- moves_factors("my_rateperdistance.csv", "my_movesrun.csv")
saveRDS(x, "my_moves_factors.rds")

# This file can be copied to an R installation on another OS.
x <- readRDS("my_moves_factors.rds")
f <- ef_moves("NOx", model_year = 2020, factors = x,
              select = list(MOVESRunID = 1, yearID = 2025, hourID = 1))
```

This interface currently accepts running exhaust (process 1), road types 2--5,
and pollutant mass rates. Starts, evaporation, stationary idle and energy need
their own rate bases and activity denominators. MOVES base operating-mode rates
also need activity weighting and adjustments before they become distance-based
factors.

EPA describes external use of rate tables in section 4.2.2 of the
[MOVES6 technical guidance](https://www.epa.gov/moves/latest-version-motor-vehicle-emission-simulator-moves).
